classification.difficultyReason: Choose suitable common powers for three different root comparisons and use order preservation for positive numbers without decimal approximations.

content.prompt: Show that $\sqrt[7]{7}<\sqrt[5]{5}<\sqrt{2}<\sqrt[3]{3}$ without using a calculator.

answer.worked:
All four roots are positive, so raising them to the same positive integer power preserves their order.

For the first pair, use the power $35$:
$$\begin{align*}(\sqrt[7]{7})^{35}&=7^5=16807\\(\sqrt[5]{5})^{35}&=5^7=78125.\end{align*}$$
Since $16807<78125$, $\sqrt[7]{7}<\sqrt[5]{5}$.

For the next pair, use the power $10$:
$$\begin{align*}(\sqrt[5]{5})^{10}&=25\\(\sqrt{2})^{10}&=32.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\sqrt[5]{5}<\sqrt{2}$.

For the last pair, use the power $6$:
$$\begin{align*}(\sqrt{2})^6&=8\\(\sqrt[3]{3})^6&=9.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\sqrt{2}<\sqrt[3]{3}$, completing the required chain.
